title: Making the Signs Known
note: He, she and her friend each make their hidden intent known to one another. This happens once he has come back and they are together, so the chapter follows the one on longing to meet.

couplets.plain: Though you hide it, your kohl-dark eyes slip your control and refuse. There is something they want to say.
couplets.pm: You say nothing and hide it, but your eyes won’t agree. They slip from your control, and there is something they are trying to tell me. Now say it plainly yourself. Hiding here means holding back out of modesty. She has changed because she thinks he means to leave. He sees it from her signs, and lets her know he doesn’t.
couplets.context: Reunited, he shows her fresh delight for many days, and she fears it means something. He reads this from her signs and speaks to her.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: your kohl-dark eyes slip your control

couplets.plain: This simple girl, with beauty that fills my eyes and arms like bamboo, has a woman’s nature in great measure.
couplets.pm: Your simple girl, whose beauty fills my eyes and whose arms are like bamboo, has more than the simple-mindedness that fills all women. He says this because she takes on herself a parting that doesn’t exist, and fears it.
couplets.note: பெண்நிறைந்த நீர்மை is the nature that fills a woman. He takes it as simple-mindedness, because she fears a parting that isn’t coming.
couplets.context: Out of modesty she won’t say it, so he speaks to her friend.
couplets.speaker: he

links.remove: The Tamil praises a woman’s nature, which he reads as simple-mindedness. Reserve came from the old English.

links.quote: beauty that fills my eyes and arms like bamboo

couplets.plain: Like the thread that shows through a bead, something shows through this young woman’s adornment.
couplets.pm: Like the thread that lies inside a strung crystal bead and shows outside, a sign lies within this young woman’s beauty and shows outside. The beauty is what comes from their union, and the sign doesn’t belong with it, yet it is there. I can’t make it out, and you must find out and tell me.
couplets.context: He goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: Like the thread that shows through a bead
links.reason: A concealed thought shows through her as thread shows through a bead, hidden and seen at once.

couplets.plain: As fragrance lies inside a closed bud, something lies inside the budding smile of this simple girl.
couplets.pm: As fragrance lies in a swelling bud and doesn’t show outside, a sign lies in the swelling smile your simple girl means to give me, and it doesn’t show outside. The swelling comes from ripeness, and the smile comes from the joy of union.
couplets.context: He goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: something lies inside the budding smile
links.reason: A budding smile carries a meaning without yet giving it, which is how lovers speak.

links.quote: As fragrance lies inside a closed bud

couplets.plain: The stealth of the woman in close-set bangles, done and gone past me, holds a medicine for the great pain I feel.
couplets.pm: She of the close-set bangles has taken something into her mind that isn’t in me, and has hidden from me because of it. That hidden sign holds the medicine for my pain. What she took in is a parting, and what she hides is a resolve to go with me. My pain comes from doing good and getting harm. The medicine is for you to assure her there is no parting.
couplets.context: He goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: The stealth of the woman in close-set bangles

couplets.plain: He comforts me so fully and joins me so gladly, but in it I see myself bearing pain again and thinking he has no love.
couplets.pm: He has come and eased the pain of parting, and he joins me so that I rejoice. Yet as things stand, this holds in it that I will bear that pain again, with difficulty, and think of his lack of love. It comes from his intent to leave, so in the end it turns bitter.
couplets.context: She has read his intent, and she tells it to her friend, who has come to reassure her.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: in it I see myself bearing pain again

couplets.plain: My bangles knew before we did that the man of the cool shore had drawn away.
couplets.pm: The man of the cool shore is with me in body, but in his mind he has parted from me. I should know this from his signs, but these bangles knew first. His intent is already formed, so she says he has drawn away. Her arms thinned before she clearly understood, and she puts that on the bangles and speaks as if they could feel.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: My bangles knew before we did
links.reason: Her bangles know he has drawn away before she does.

couplets.plain: It was only yesterday my lover left, and I have been pale in body for seven days.
couplets.pm: My lover went only yesterday, and I have been pale over it for seven days. The tenderness he showed yesterday told me his parting was decided, so she says he left yesterday. She has suspected it for seven days and turned pale that first day, so she says seven. In this way she makes his intent to leave known.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: pale in body for seven days
links.reason: Her body has been pale for seven days, over a man gone for one.

couplets.plain: She looked at her bangles, looked at her soft arms, looked at her feet. That is what she did there.
couplets.pm: I reassured her and she wasn’t reassured. She looked at her bangles: if he leaves and I stay, these won’t stay on. She looked at her soft arms, which will thin and cause it. She looked at her feet: you must walk and save me from both. So what she did there was a sign that she will go with you. If you mean to leave, it is there to stop you.
couplets.context: Her friend has read her signs, and she makes them known to him.
couplets.speaker: maid

links.quote: She looked at her bangles, looked at her soft arms, looked at her feet.
That is what she did there.
links.reason: The maid acts as go-between, passing her mistress’s silent signs on to him.

couplets.plain: To tell the sickness of desire with the eyes and beg: they say this is womanhood on top of womanhood.
couplets.pm: Women don’t speak their sickness of desire even to their friends. They tell it with their eyes, and instead of begging friends to end it, they beg their own feet to go with him. Those who know call this a womanhood beyond their natural womanhood. Hearing her resolve from the friend, he praises it as if of others, and shows he won’t leave.
couplets.context: He makes it known to her friend that he doesn’t mean to leave.
couplets.speaker: he

links.reason: Admires a woman who will plead the sickness of desire with her eyes but won’t say it aloud.

links.quote: To tell the sickness of desire with the eyes and beg
